derivative-in-context-s1.title: Depth of snow on a deck

table.caption: Depth D(t) of snow on a deck, in centimeters, at selected times t, in hours after the snow began

plot.label: Graph of P(t) = 0.5 t squared + 1, the number of bacteria in thousands, for t from 0 to 6 hours, with the tangent line at t = 3 passing through (3, 5.5) and (5, 11.5)

items.q: $D$ is differentiable. Use the data in the table to estimate $D'(5.5)$. Include units.

mistakes.why: The subtraction is reversed. Later minus earlier, over later minus earlier: $\frac{21.1 - 20.0}{6 - 5}$.
That is the average rate over the whole table, $\frac{24 - 12}{10}$. Use the closest times on each side of 5.5.

why.correct: Use the two times that straddle 5.5: $D'(5.5) \approx \frac{D(6) - D(5)}{6 - 5} = \frac{21.1 - 20.0}{1} = 1.1$ centimeters per hour.

options: centimeters per hour
centimeters
hours per centimeter
centimeters times hours

why.correct: A derivative is a change in output over a change in input: $\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{hr}}$, centimeters per hour.
options: Output units (centimeters) per input unit (hours).
Those are the units of $D(t)$, the depth itself.
The ratio is upside down: the output change goes on top.
A rate divides the output units by the input units.

items.q: Estimate $D'(8)$ using the table. Include units.

mistakes.why: That is the change in depth, $24.0 - 21.1$. Divide by the change in time, $10 - 6 = 4$ hours.
The interval from $t = 6$ to $t = 10$ is 4 hours wide, not 2; the table's widths are unequal.

items.q: From the table, $D'(3) \approx 1.6$. Which is the best interpretation?
options: In the first 3 hours, the depth of the snow increased by about 1.6 centimeters
At 3 hours, the depth of the snow is increasing at about 1.6 centimeters per hour
At 3 hours, the snow on the deck is about 1.6 centimeters deep
Over the first 3 hours, the snow fell at an average of 1.6 centimeters per hour

why.correct: An interpretation names the instant, the quantity, whether it increases or decreases, and the units: at $t = 3$ hours the depth is increasing at about 1.6 cm per hour.
options: That describes a change over an interval, in centimeters; $D'(3)$ is a rate at $t = 3$.
A derivative is a rate at one instant, with units of depth per time.
That would be $D(3)$, a depth; the table puts the depth between 15.2 and 20 centimeters then.
$D'(3)$ is the rate at the instant $t = 3$, not an average from 0 to 3.

items.q: The graph shows the number of bacteria $P(t)$, in thousands, $t$ hours after a culture started, and the line tangent to the graph at $t = 3$. Find $P'(3)$ with units.

mistakes.why: That is $P(3)$, the height of the graph. $P'(3)$ is the slope of the tangent line.
That is the average rate from $t = 1$ to $t = 3$, the slope of a secant line, not of the tangent line.

why.correct: $P'(3)$ is the slope of the tangent line: $\frac{11.5 - 5.5}{5 - 3} = 3$ thousand bacteria per hour.

items.q: How does $P'(3)$ compare with the average rate of change of $P$ from $t = 1$ to $t = 3$?
options: $P'(3)$ equals the average rate, since both use $t = 3$
$P'(3)$ is less than the average rate, which is $4$
$P'(3)$ is greater: 3 versus an average of 2
They are not comparable, because their units differ

why.correct: The slope of the tangent line is 3; the secant from $(1, 1.5)$ to $(3, 5.5)$ has slope 2. The population grows faster at $t = 3$ than on average before it.
options: The average rate is the slope of a secant line through two points; it is 2, not 3.
That divides $5.5 - 1.5 = 4$ by 1 instead of by 2 hours.
The average rate is $\frac{5.5 - 1.5}{3 - 1} = 2$.
Both are in thousand bacteria per hour.
After 3 hours, there are 3 thousand bacteria
Each hour, the population triples
During the first 3 hours, a total of 3 thousand bacteria were added to the culture
At 3 hours, the population is growing at 3 thousand bacteria per hour

why.correct: $P'(3) = 3$ means that at $t = 3$ hours the number of bacteria is increasing at 3 thousand bacteria per hour.
options: That would mean $P(3) = 3$; the graph shows $P(3) = 5.5$.
The derivative measures a rate of change in thousands per hour, not a growth factor.
That is a total change over an interval; $P'(3)$ is a rate at one instant.
Instant, quantity, direction and units are all named.

items.q: Which of these quantities has units of thousands of bacteria, not thousands of bacteria per hour?
options: The slope of the tangent line at $t = 3$

why.correct: Values of $P$ are counts (thousands); slopes, derivatives and difference quotients are rates (thousands per hour).
options: A value of $P$ is a number of bacteria, in thousands.
A derivative of $P$ is a rate, in thousands per hour.
A slope on this graph is thousands per hour.
A change in $P$ divided by a time is a rate.

items.q: The volume of a balloon is $V(r)$ cubic centimeters when its radius is $r$ centimeters. What are the units of $V'(r)$?
options: cubic centimeters
cubic centimeters per centimeter
centimeters per cubic centimeter
cubic centimeters per second

why.correct: $V'(r) = \frac{dV}{dr}$ has units of $V$ over units of $r$: cubic centimeters per centimeter.
options: Those are the units of $V(r)$.
Output units (cm³) per input unit (cm).
That is the reciprocal: the output change goes on top.
The input here is the radius, not time.

items.q: $W(t)$ is the number of liters of water in a tank $t$ minutes after noon. What does $W'(20) = -4$ mean?
options: At 12:20 there are 4 liters of water in the tank
In the first 20 minutes the tank lost 4 liters
At 12:20 the volume is decreasing at 4 liters per minute
At 12:20 the amount of water is decreasing at 4 minutes per liter

why.correct: $W'(20) = -4$ liters per minute: at $t = 20$ minutes the volume is decreasing at 4 liters per minute.
options: That would be $W(20) = 4$.
That is a change over an interval; $W'(20)$ is a rate at one instant.
A negative rate means the amount is going down.
The units are upside down: liters per minute.

items.q: $C(x)$ is the cost, in dollars, of producing $x$ bicycles. What does $C'(100) = 85$ tell you?
options: Producing 100 bicycles costs 85 dollars
Each of the first 100 bicycles cost 85 dollars
The cost goes up by 85 dollars for each 100 bicycles
Producing one more bicycle after the 100th costs about 85 dollars

why.correct: $C'(100)$ is in dollars per bicycle. Near $x = 100$, one more bicycle adds about 85 dollars to the cost.
options: That would be $C(100) = 85$.
That is an average over 100 bicycles, not the rate at $x = 100$.
The rate is per one bicycle, the input unit.
A rate of 85 dollars per bicycle near $x = 100$.

items.q: A ball is thrown upward. Its height is $h(t) = 40t - 5t^2$ meters, $t$ seconds after the throw. Find $h'(2)$ with units.

mistakes.why: That is $h(2) = 80 - 20$, the height. The question asks for the rate of change.
The derivative of $5t^2$ is $10t$, which is 20 at $t = 2$: $40 - 20 = 20$.

why.correct: $h'(t) = 40 - 10t$, so $h'(2) = 20$ meters per second: at $t = 2$ the ball is rising at 20 meters per second.

items.q: A square has side $s$ centimeters and area $A(s) = s^2$ square centimeters. Find $A'(5)$ with units.

mistakes.why: That is $A(5)$, the area. The derivative is $A'(5) = 2(5)$.

why.correct: $A'(s) = 2s$, so $A'(5) = 10$ square centimeters per centimeter: near $s = 5$, the area grows about 10 cm² for each extra centimeter of side.

items.q: $H(t)$ is the height, in feet, of a tree $t$ years after it was planted. Which statement means the same as $H'(4) > H'(8)$?
options: The tree was growing faster at 4 years than at 8 years
The tree was taller at 4 years than at 8 years
The tree grew more from year 4 to year 8 than before year 4
The tree was shrinking between 4 and 8 years

why.correct: $H'(t)$ is a growth rate, measured in feet per year. $H'(4) > H'(8)$ says the tree grew faster at 4 years than at 8 years.
options: Derivatives compare rates of growth, in feet per year.
That compares heights, $H(4) > H(8)$.
That compares changes over intervals, not rates at two instants.
Both rates may be positive; one is just smaller.

items.q: $W(t)$ is the weight, in kilograms, of a calf $t$ days after birth, and $W'(10) = 0.8$. About how much weight does the calf gain from day 10 to day 12?
options: About 0.8 kilograms
About 1.6 kilograms
About 8 kilograms
About 12.8 kilograms

why.correct: Over a short time, change $\approx$ rate $\times$ time: $0.8 \text{ kg per day} \times 2 \text{ days} = 1.6$ kg.
options: That is one day's worth at this rate; the interval is 2 days.
0.8 kilograms per day for 2 days.
That multiplies by 10, the day number, instead of by the 2 days that pass.
That multiplies by 12 instead of by the 2-day change in time.
